sources.title: Introducing Mercury 2
sources.evidence: Launch announcement names Mercury 2, explains parallel diffusion refinement, and lists tunable reasoning, 128K context, native tool use and JSON output. It announces immediate API and chat availability. Freshly reopened October 27; the full announcement publishes no total or active parameter count and identifies no sized unchanged base.

sources.title: Inception Blog
sources.evidence: The official index dates Introducing Mercury 2 to February 24, 2026. The separate Azure announcement is dated June 24, 2026.

sources.title: Models - Inception Platform
sources.evidence: The exact Mercury 2 row lists chat completions, 128K context, 50,000 maximum output tokens, tool calling, structured outputs and text format. It is separate from Mercury 2.5, Mercury 3 and Mercury Edit 2. Reopened October 27; the exact Mercury 2 specification row still gives serving capabilities, not parameter counts.

sources.title: List available models - Inception Platform
sources.evidence: The documented mercury-2 model object names Inception: Mercury 2, specifies context_length 128000, text input/output, and tools support. This is a documentation example, not a live authenticated endpoint check; its repeated created timestamp is not used as release evidence.

sources.title: Frequently Asked Questions - Inception Platform
sources.evidence: The FAQ explicitly includes Mercury 2 among models accepting only text input and states that image generation is unsupported.

sources.title: Reasoning Efforts - Inception Platform
sources.evidence: The reasoning_effort control explicitly applies to mercury-2, with instant, low, medium and high settings; its documented default is medium.

sources.title: Mercury 2: the first reasoning model fast enough to pick up the phone
sources.evidence: This later Mercury 2 article explains the Mercury denoising model as a standard Transformer trained to predict clean text across sequence positions simultaneously. It describes Mercury 2 reasoning controls and its role as the text LLM in an ASR/LLM/TTS voice pipeline. It does not specify dense/MoE structure or parameter counts. Reopened October 27; denoising and shared weight loading across many tokens are not a numerical active-count convention.

sources.title: Terms of Use
sources.evidence: Terms effective September 1, 2025 identify Inception AI, Inc. as owner of the services, grant restricted service-use rights and prohibit unauthorized redistribution, modification and reverse engineering. These support the descriptive proprietary license classification, not a named open-weight license.

sources.title: Mercury 2 on Azure Foundry
sources.evidence: The exact Mercury 2 deployment announcement describes a paid hourly software license separate from compute and links an Azure model card. This is a licensed deployment route, not an open-weight release.

sources.title: Mercury-2 version 1 model card - Microsoft Foundry
sources.evidence: Followed the card linked by Inception; the retrieval returned a Microsoft Foundry shell with no readable content. No technical or license claim is attributed to its unavailable body. Reopened October 27; the same exact-model URL again returned an empty readable shell, so no count is inferred from it.

sources.title: Mercury: Ultra-Fast Language Models Based on Diffusion
sources.evidence: The technical report linked by Inception covers the earlier Mercury Coder Mini and Small models and Transformer denoising. It contains no Mercury 2 model specification; its earlier-model details are not transferred to Mercury 2. Reread the complete first-party report from the freshly fetched October 27 cache; mathematical parameter notation and comparator model sizes do not disclose a count for Mercury 2.

sources.title: Diffusion at Scale: Introducing Mercury 3
sources.evidence: The later announcement discusses total-parameter scaling relative to Mercury 1 Mini and includes a chart labeled M2. It supplies no absolute Mercury 2 total or active parameter count and no Mercury 2 dense/MoE disclosure. Freshly reopened October 27; the explicit more-than-40x claim concerns Mercury 3 versus Mercury 1 Mini, not an absolute count for Mercury 2.

sources.title: Model Quality vs. Model Size - Mercury 3 announcement figure
sources.evidence: Visually inspected the first-party figure. M2 is explicitly labeled February 2026, but the horizontal axis gives total parameters relative to Mercury 1 Mini on a log scale. Neither an absolute count nor a numeric M2 ratio is printed. No count is inferred from chart position.

sources.title: Introducing Mercury 2.5
sources.evidence: The later release compares Mercury 2.5 with Mercury 2 on quality and deployment experience, but gives no numeric Mercury 2 parameter count, active count or expert structure. The successor's 260K context is not applied to Mercury 2. Reopened October 27; the successor comparison gives neither a transferable Mercury 2 size nor an unchanged-checkpoint relationship.

sources.title: Research - Inception
sources.evidence: Reviewed the official research index and its Mercury technical-report link. No Mercury 2-specific technical report or model-card parameter table was found there; exact-name searches also found no first-party numeric count. Freshly reopened October 27; the current research index still links the June 2025 Mercury report, without a later Mercury 2 count.

sources.title: Our Models - Inception
sources.evidence: Current model page says Mercury 2 and 2.5 are unavailable to new users, with pre-October 19 customers retaining access until November 15, 2026; enterprise support follows their agreements. This limits availability claims despite the model remaining documented.

sources.title: Mercury 2 benchmark and estimated model facts
sources.evidence: Fresh October 27 numeric lead explicitly labels approximately 100B an estimate and states that parameter topology/count are undisclosed. Its Parameter source link resolves only to Inception’s homepage, which supplies no count. Original benchmark measurements do not substantiate this architectural estimate; rejected as a parameter specification.

sources.title: Unlocking Lossless Speedups in LLMs via Discrete Diffusion
sources.publisher: Sahoo et al. / Institute of Foundation Models, Cerebras and academic collaborators
sources.evidence: Freshly retrieved and read the complete September 3, 2026 original Uno research PDF after its HTML URL returned 404. Section 5.1.1 explicitly states Mercury 2’s parameter count is undisclosed; Table 1 lists its model size as N/A while listing numeric sizes for Uno, DiffusionGemma and Nemotron-Labs-Diffusion. No Mercury 2 active-count row or component/phase size is supplied. This later original model-team comparison corroborates the missing disclosure rather than furnishing an estimate.

name.note: The announcement and exact mercury-2 API identifier agree on the model name.

developer.note: Inception announces its own model; the terms identify the company as Inception AI, Inc.

family.note: The later first-party Mercury generation chart explicitly includes M2 between the first and later generations. Lowercase matches the catalog family key.

release_date.note: The official index dates the launch to February 24, and that launch announces immediate availability. June Azure distribution and later provider listings are not the original release.

open_weights.note: Official distribution is through controlled API/chat access and commercial deployments under restrictive terms. No public weight download or open-weight license was found in the reviewed primary material.

license.note: Descriptive classification supported by restricted service-use terms and the exact model's paid deployment license; this is not an SPDX or open-weight license designation.

parameters_b.note: October 27 fresh exact-name/ID searches for total parameters, billion-scale sizes, technical reports and later primary comparisons found no supported nominal total. Reopened the launch, exact specifications, research index, original report and later Mercury 2.5/3 releases. No named sized base or unchanged-weight lineage is documented. The generation chart is relative to an undisclosed Mercury 1 Mini size; it cannot yield an absolute Mercury 2 count. AI BENCHY’s approximately 100B lead is explicitly an estimate and cites a homepage with no number. The later original Uno report explicitly lists Mercury 2 size as N/A. Azure’s exact card body remains unreadable. Retain null, without requiring an exact tensor census for a future nominal disclosure.

active_parameters_b.note: October 27 searches separately checked active/activated parameters and original comparison tables, including arXiv, NVIDIA and Azure sources. Reopened first-party diffusion/Transformer explanations and inspected the later Uno comparison. None publishes a numerical Mercury 2 active-count convention, expert configuration or component count. Parallel token refinement and shared weight loading do not imply a number, and neither throughput nor a sibling model’s size supports an inference. Explicitly retain null.

architecture.note: The launch establishes diffusion generation; the later Mercury 2 explanation identifies the denoising network as a standard Transformer. Dense versus MoE, layer counts and expert configuration remain undisclosed.

context_window.note: The model table's 128K is resolved explicitly to 128000 in the exact mercury-2 documented model object. Maximum output is a separate 50000-token limit.

modalities.note: The exact model object specifies text input/output, and the FAQ expressly excludes image input for Mercury 2. Voice applications use surrounding speech components.

reasoning.note: The exact mercury-2 endpoint supports instant, low, medium and high reasoning effort, with medium documented as default.

tool_call.note: Both the Mercury 2 model table and exact model object's supported_features explicitly include tool calling.

description.value: Mercury 2 is Inception's text-only diffusion language model with adjustable reasoning, tool calling, and a 128,000-token context window.
description.note: Replaces generic purpose language with directly documented model properties and omits comparative performance claims.

patch.description: Mercury 2 is Inception's text-only diffusion language model with adjustable reasoning, tool calling, and a 128,000-token context window.
patch.notes: Diffusion generation uses a Transformer denoising network. No total or active parameter count was found in the checked primary sources; the later Mercury size chart is relative only. Dense/MoE details remain undisclosed. As of October 26, 2026, Inception documents Mercury 2 but restricts it to existing customers until November 15, with enterprise support governed by agreements; endpoint operation was not tested.

sources.label: Exact model object and context length

summary: October 27 parameter re-audit retains explicit null total and active counts after fresh original-source, named-base and later-comparison searches. Rejected the approximately 100B aggregator estimate because its cited source supplies no count. The September Uno original research comparison explicitly records Mercury 2 size as N/A; the Mercury 3 chart remains relative. No unchanged sized base is documented. All twelve unrelated assessments and earlier corrections are preserved.
